checks: Checked original 942ae5a91bb1a792 §§3–4, (6)–(10), against the frozen source. The proposed proof replaces the distributional second-derivative argument with affine supports, and keeps the same sequence and actual selector.

A finite nonnegative convex nondecreasing g on the closed half-line is right-continuous at zero by convexity and monotonicity. Its affine supports at positive arguments have nonnegative slopes and their supremum also gives the endpoint value. Multiplying the support formula by a nonnegative argument yields a supremum of convex quadratics for t g(lambda t). That function is nondecreasing since both factors are nonnegative and nondecreasing. Composition with the positive part therefore makes k convex and nondecreasing on the line.

The affine supports of k have nonnegative slopes. Thus t k(log t-T) is a supremum of convex functions m t log t plus a linear term. The perspective b times this function at a/b is jointly convex on positive pairs. It increases in a by positivity and monotonicity of k, and decreases in b by monotonicity of k. These two signs justify composition with convex f and concave L_j, then a nonnegative globally finite extension by the same support construction as in the floor proof.

For fixed positive shifted f and fixed T, c=T-log f is positive and bounded on the common physical compact set. On the support of the test ell_j>c, so the logarithmic term has the positive rate r_j. The stated expansion follows by adding and subtracting v_j g(r_j) and then the constant g(0) term. Each error is bounded by Lip(g) lambda_j c s_j because 0<=v_j<=s_j and s_j-v_j<=c. The bounded rate range gives the required Lipschitz bound even at zero, by monotonicity and a secant to a larger positive argument.

The expansion's error in the W_j-beta_j contribution integrates to zero by the uniformly bounded first log mass. The truncation min(s_j,c) is a bounded continuous function of L_j and w after extending it by c at zero, hence passes using the two given selector weak limits. It removes exactly the ordinary truncated term and leaves the residual a minus beta times b with g(r).

In the logarithmic term multiply the same expansion by r_j. The bounded rate controls its error, and the truncated correction is bounded by a constant times lambda_j s_j. The remaining lifted integrand has multiplier r g(r), continuous and bounded on the rate interval. Its ordinary part is zero. The R_j term vanishes since |R_j|<=C lambda_j and the test is bounded by a constant times s_j.

Take the subsequential weak limit first at fixed T and fixed positive shift. Then T tending to infinity removes the ordinary integral by integrable domination by the positive log, and the positive shift tends to zero against finite measures. Powers r^m and the constant one are valid weights. For g(r)=(r-t)_+, use r(r-t)_+=t(r-t)_++(r-t)_+^2 to get the stated tail inequality, including t=beta. This uses allowed integrated tests and does not derive a pointwise selector bound.
